text:
alex: kicking off TideWorks RFI thread. they want an end-to-end POC: embeddings + semantic search, Private option with HSM, SSO (SAML), and 99th pctl latency targets. deadline next Wed. who picks matrix + sec answers?

meera: I can do security Qs. please drop the RFI PDF. need to see section on data flows and retention asks.

alex: uploaded to drive: https://drive.redwood/tideworks/tideworks_rfi_v3.pdf. they list peak embed QPS 150, sustained 40, avg tokens 12, long context up to 2048 tokens.

tony: 150 peak is nontrivial. Hosted with caching+batching ok; Dedicated or Private needs at least 3x L4 baseline or burst to H100 for tails. for initial POC recommend Hosted Dedicated pool with KV caching enabled.

meera: security checklist highlights: customer-managed KMS & HSM (FIPS 140-2), SOC2, SCIM & SAML, detailed retention policies. I'll draft answers.

alex: customer asked for run-rate pricing (monthly) for: Hosted managed, Dedicated reserved, and Private one-time infra + support. can pricing-bot give ballpark?

pricing-bot: roughs: Hosted managed w/ caching & autoscale: ~$15k/mo (est 50M tokens/mo). Dedicated reserved (3x L4 baseline): ~$38k/mo + instance ops. Private: one-time infra & deployment ~$120k, monthly support ~$9k. mark as estimates.

meera: HSM lead time question: they expect <2 weeks. Can we meet that?

tony: HSM lead time is vendor-dependent. realistic: 3-4 weeks for procurement + validation. add note in RFI: "HSM available for Private; estimated provisioning 3+ weeks."

alex: they also want explicit latency numbers for embeddings at 12 tokens and 2048 tokens (99th pctl). include both Hosted cached and Private baseline.

tony: suggested latency numbers: "Embeddings 12t: 99th pctl 50ms (Hosted cached), 110ms (Dedicated baseline)" and "Embeddings 2048t: 99th pctl 320ms (Hosted cached), 760ms (Dedicated baseline)". note KV cache reduces tail latencies in practice.

meera: data retention phrasing: `Hosted: request metadata retained 30 days by default; payloads redacted unless customer opts in. Private: full control over retention and logging.` Add export control line: `Standard U.S. export controls apply; recommend Private for restricted regimes.`

alex: they asked about fallback policy if Dedicated pool is saturated. include graceful degradation statement.

tony: add: "Graceful degradation: automated routing to quantized compatible variant in same region, configurable rate-limits, and prioritized canary fallback to maintain availability."

pricing-bot: adding an ops note: Dedicated requires monitoring integration and optionally APM agents for SLA. SLA available post-contract; POC is best-effort.

meera: function/tool-calling in Private? they need callbacks to internal webhooks.

tony: Private supports tool-calls via agents bridge and outbound webhooks; customers must whitelist destinations and provide network egress rules. doc: https://docs.redwood/private-tooling.

alex: please attach a capability matrix CSV and a short test curl for their engs.

pricing-bot: uploaded draft matrix: https://files.redwood/cap-matrix/tideworks_matrix_draft.csv :thumbsup:

tony: curl snippet for the thread:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: tide-smoke-1" \
  -d '{"model":"r-instruct-emb-1","input":"hello world"}'
```

meera: I'll compile security answers and upload a short PDF with references to SOC2, encryption, KMS, and HSM lead times.

alex: legal wants export controls verified before sending. pinged @legal.

meera: final checklist: matrix with latency rows, pricing estimates, HSM caveat, retention language, fallback policy, and test curl. I'll assemble the RFI bundle and circulate.

tony: one ops addendum: include network peering checklist and NTP/time-sync requirement for HSM.

alex: thanks team. aiming to send bundle Tue morning. flag blockers now. :rocket:
